The reason /tmp is choking is because /tmp is a tmpfs living in RAM (capped at 32GB and 1M inodes by default), and you have persistent git worktrees (/tmp/workflow-wt-*), docs, and branch checkouts sitting in it.
To keep all workflows intact without deleting anything, you have two clean options:
Option 1: Instantly Expand /tmp (Fastest, zero moves)
Because awrawr-pc has 62GB RAM and 200GB swap, you can immediately double the tmpfs size and quadrupled the inode limit on the fly without rebooting or touching a single file:
sudo mount -o remount,size=64G,nr_inodes=4M /tmp

Verify with:
df -h /tmp
df -i /tmp

 * Effect: Takes effect in 0 seconds. Gives you 64GB and 4 million inodes backed by your RAM + 200GB swap pool. Nothing is deleted.
Option 2: Migrate Workflows to NVMe & Symlink Back (Best long-term)
If you want these worktrees to persist across reboots and stop consuming physical RAM/tmpfs inodes, move them to your 277GB NVMe partition (~/.local/share/worktrees) and leave symlinks in /tmp so any active processes looking for /tmp/workflow-wt-* don't break:
# 1. Create persistent directory on NVMe
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/worktrees

# 2. Move worktrees to disk and create symlinks back to /tmp
for d in /tmp/workflow-wt-* /tmp/hatch-docs /tmp/bl-fix3; do
    [ -e "$d" ] || continue
    name="$(basename "$d")"
    mv "$d" ~/.local/share/worktrees/
    ln -s "$HOME/.local/share/worktrees/$name" "/tmp/$name"
done

# 3. Verify reclaimed tmpfs space and active links
df -h /tmp
df -i /tmp
ls -l /tmp/workflow-wt-*

Preventing New Workflows from Landing in /tmp
Whatever runner spawned workflow-wt-* (e.g. OpenClaw, git-worktree script, or Ralph) defaults to /tmp because $TMPDIR is unset or hardcoded. You can set:
export TMPDIR="$HOME/.local/state/tmp"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"

in ~/.bashrc.env so future agent worktrees automatically allocate on your 277GB NVMe partition instead of your RAM-backed tmpfs.
